title: Virus nucleic acids extractions from 0.02 µm anotop filters
author: Jozef Nissimov

materials: Luer-Lok female–female adapter fittings (Waters; catalog # WAT011422)

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL of the supplied Proteinase K to 1 mL of either X1 or X2 T+C lysis solution to obtain a final Proteinase K concentration of 100 µg mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Thaw filters and remove parafilm
steps.instruction: Thaw the Anotop 0.02 µm syringe filters at room temperature for 5 minutes and peel off the parafilm coating from both inlet and outlet.

steps.title: Remove residual water from filters
steps.instruction: Knock each filter gently on kimwipe paper a few times with the outlet facing down to eliminate remaining water from the filter housing.

steps.title: Load extraction buffer into injection syringe
steps.instruction: Pipette 1 mL of the prepared extraction buffer into a sterile 3 mL BD syringe that has been fitted with a female‑female Luer‑Lok adapter (the injection syringe).

steps.title: Connect injection syringe and inject buffer
steps.instruction: Ensure minimal air in the syringe‑adapter assembly, connect it to the filter outlet, hold the assembly vertically with the syringe pushing upward, and gently push the buffer until liquid first appears at the filter inlet (do not lose this liquid).

substeps.instruction: Check for and remove any air bubbles in the syringe‑adapter line.
Attach the injection syringe to the filter outlet.
Push buffer upward until liquid emerges from the inlet.

steps.title: Attach aspiration syringe to filter inlet
steps.instruction: Connect a second sterile 3 mL BD syringe (the aspiration syringe) to the filter inlet.

steps.title: Incubate assembly at 65 °C
steps.instruction: Secure the filter with both syringes to a rotisserie using elastic bands, place the assembly in a hybridization oven set to 65 °C, and incubate for 15 minutes at rotor speed 5 (or equivalent low speed) to ensure full wetting of the filter surface.

steps.title: Cool assembly and collect extract
steps.instruction: Remove the assembly from the oven, let it cool briefly at room temperature, then hold it vertically with the aspiration syringe below (filter upside down) and gently pull the plunger to draw the extract into the aspiration syringe.

steps.title: Transfer extract to microcentrifuge tube
steps.instruction: Detach the aspiration syringe carefully to avoid back‑flush pressure and dispense the extract (≈1 mL) into a sterile 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Chill extract on ice
steps.instruction: Place the 2 mL tube on ice for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Add MPC precipitation reagent and vortex
steps.instruction: Add one‑half volume (~500 µL) of MPC protein precipitation reagent (from the kit) to the chilled extract and vortex for 10 seconds.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet debris
steps.instruction: Spin the mixture at 13,000 rpm for 15 minutes at 4 °C to pellet cellular debris.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant (optional freeze)
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the clear supernatant to a new sterile 2 mL tube, avoiding the pellet; the sample may be stored at –80 °C at this point if desired.

steps.title: Add polyacryl carrier to sample
steps.instruction: Transfer 800 µL of the supernatant to a fresh sterile 2 mL tube, add 1 µL polyacryl carrier, and vortex briefly.

steps.title: Add isopropanol and mix
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume (~800 µL) of 100 % isopropanol, then invert the tube 10–40 times to mix.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 13,000 rpm for 45 minutes (longer times may improve yield for low‑quantity samples).

steps.title: Decant supernatant carefully
steps.instruction: Carefully decant or aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the nucleic‑acid pellet.

steps.title: Wash pellet twice with ethanol
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet twice with 1 mL of 70 % ethanol, centrifuging 1 minute each wash; then either decant the pellet until dry in a hood or gently aspirate residual ethanol with a pipette.

steps.title: Air‑dry pellet and dissolve in TE
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet, then dissolve it in 35 µL of 0.02‑µm‑filtered sterile TE buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 1 mM EDTA) pre‑heated to 50 °C.

steps.title: Optional enzymatic removal of DNA or RNA
steps.instruction: If desired, treat the total nucleic‑acid solution with DNase or RNase to selectively remove DNA or RNA, respectively.
